title: docs(agents): point PD #12 at the alias retirement path, not two stale examples
body:
One sentence in AGENTS.md Prime Directive #12. Found while auditing the alias debt that directive names, as the sweep #3754 asked for.

## The problem

PD #12 currently reads:

> The existing `cfg.filter ?? cfg.filters` / `cfg.objectName ?? cfg.object` in the flow executors are **debt to pay down, not a pattern to copy**.

Neither still looks like that, so an agent who greps for them finds nothing — and learns nothing about how the debt is actually being retired:

- **`filters` → `filter` has graduated** into the ADR-0087 D2 conversion layer (`flow-node-crud-filter-alias`). It is rewritten to the canonical key **at load**, including the `AutomationEngine.registerFlow` rehydration seam — which is precisely the stored-prod-flow gap a publish-time lint cannot reach. The CRUD executors now read `cfg.filter` directly; no consumer-side fallback survives.
- **`object` → `objectName` is mid-retirement** behind `readAliasedConfig` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/config-aliases.ts`): canonical wins, the alias keeps already-stored flows running, and each alias warns once so authors get steered off it. Its own doc block names graduation into the conversion layer as the next step.

The directive was pointing at the symptom after the cure had been designed and half-applied.

## The change

Rewrites the sentence to teach the **mechanism** rather than name two moved examples: tolerate an alias only behind the shim (never a bare `??`) so it is declared, warned, lintable by `graph-lint`, and *removable on a schedule* — then graduate it into the conversion layer. Points at #3796 for the call sites still open-coded.

Docs only — no code, no behavior change.

## Verified while writing it

- Only `AGENTS.md` carried this sentence as a live claim. `docs/adr/0087` also mentions `cfg.filter ?? cfg.filters`, but as a *historical example of the banned pattern* ("the scattered `cfg.filter ?? cfg.filters` pattern where each executor quietly tolerates off-spec input") — still accurate, deliberately left alone.
- The claim that `filters` is retired is from `config-aliases.ts`'s own header plus the absence of any surviving `cfg.filter ?? cfg.filters` in the tree; the `object` → `objectName` call site in `crud-nodes.ts` is the one the shim documents.

## Related

Filed from the same sweep, not fixed here:

- #3795 (P2) — `protocol.ts` implements 4 of the 5 documented `RpcQueryOptionsSchema` alias precedences backwards, disagreeing with `http-dispatcher.ts` on three.
- #3796 (P3) — six flow-node config aliases still open-coded, bypassing `readAliasedConfig`.

Refs #3754, #3796, ADR-0087
